ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Lakum deenukum wa liya deen' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted not merely as a declaration of separation but as a confirmation of the finality of Islamic monotheism against the polytheism of the Quraysh, establishing the principle of 'La Ikrah' (no compulsion) in religion. It underscores the distinct theological boundaries between the Ahl al-Haqq and the Ahl al-Batil, serving as a foundational text for religious pluralism within a monotheistic framework.
